name: Warden of Evos Isle
oracle_text:
Flying
Creature spells with flying you cast cost {1} less to cast.
blocked_sentences: Creature spells with flying you cast cost {1} less to cast.

needs.what: a static ability on a permanent that reduces the generic portion of the cost of OTHER spells its controller casts, scoped by a filter over the spell's own printed characteristics - e.g. `{"kind": "static", "effect": "spell_cost_reduction", "affects_spells": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "keywords": ["flying"]}, "amount": {"const": 1}}`. It must be read at the same choke points the existing self-reduction is (`legality.affordable`/`legality` cast enumeration and `game.cast` via `costs.cost_reduction`), so a spell offered at the reduced price is also paid at the reduced price, and it must be clamped at zero and generic-only like the existing one.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The nearest thing is the card-level `cost_reduction` field (`carddef.CardDef.cost_reduction`, `costs.cost_reduction`, `loader.COST_REDUCTION_KEYS = {count, total_power}`), and it points the other way: it reduces the cost of the card that CARRIES it, and its filter is a board filter counting permanents on the battlefield (`costs._reduction_matches` iterates `state.battlefield`). Warden reduces the cost of a different card - a creature spell with flying being cast from hand - selected by that spell's own characteristics, which `cost_reduction` has no way to name and no way to apply to anything but its own card. Writing `cost_reduction` on Warden would make Warden itself cheaper, a different card. The static vocabulary offers no alternative either: `loader.STATIC_EFFECTS` is buff / grant_keyword / set_pt / add_subtype / set_types / protection plus the player-wide extra_land_drops, no_hand_limit, play_lands_from_graveyard, play_lands_from_library_top, double_land_triggers, double_land_mana, freeze_opponent_lands - all of which describe a characteristic of a permanent or a permission of a player, none of which touches what a spell costs. The `double_land_mana` precedent shows the shape a payment-time static takes, but it doubles mana produced by lands, not the price of a spell.

needs.what: a filter form that can be matched against a spell being cast (a card in hand / on the stack) rather than against a permanent on the battlefield, reading its printed types and keywords - so "creature spells with flying" is expressible at the moment legality prices the card
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `STATIC_FILTER_KEYS` (which `_validate_cost_reduction` reuses) does carry `types` and `keywords`, but the only consumer, `costs._reduction_matches`, walks `state.battlefield` and calls `chars(state, oid)` on permanents - there is no code path that applies a filter to the card whose cost is being computed. A trigger-based stand-in (`spell_cast` with `filter: {types: ["Creature"], keywords: ["flying"]}`) cannot substitute: the trigger resolves after the spell has already been cast and paid for, so at best it could refund mana into the pool, which is not the same as being able to afford the spell in the first place and would change what `legality` offers.
